formulas.title: Fermi Beta-Decay Differential Momentum Spectrum
formulas.description: Gives the differential probability per unit time and electron momentum $p_e$ for allowed nuclear beta decay in Fermi's four-fermion contact theory, incorporating the CKM element $V_{ud}$, nuclear matrix element $\mathcal{M}_{fi}$, Coulomb Fermi function $F(Z', p_e)$, and neutrino phase space $(Q_\beta - T_e)^2$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Fermi's beta spectrum combines Fermi's Golden Rule with three-body relativistic phase space to predict the continuous momentum distribution of emitted electrons and the linearity of the Kurie plot.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Because the decay energy is split continuously between an electron and an unseen antineutrino, emitted electrons span a smooth bell-shaped spectrum whose high-energy endpoint directly weighs the neutrino.
formulas.interpretation: Derived from Fermi's Golden Rule with a point-like weak interaction $G_F V_{ud}$ (the low-energy limit of $W$-boson exchange). For massless neutrinos, the neutrino energy is $E_\nu = Q_\beta - T_e$, so $\sqrt{(d\lambda_\beta/dp_e)/(p_e^2 F)} \propto (Q_\beta - T_e)$ forms a linear Kurie plot; nonzero neutrino mass replaces $(Q_\beta - T_e)^2$ by $(Q_\beta - T_e)\sqrt{(Q_\beta - T_e)^2 - m_\nu^2 c^4}$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows from Lorentz-invariant three-body phase space and the effective low-energy $SU(2)_L$ charged-current weak four-fermion interaction.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Vanishes at zero electron momentum ($p_e \to 0$) and at the kinematic endpoint ($T_e \to Q_\beta$). For $Z' = 0$ (free neutron decay), $F(0, p_e) = 1$; for heavy nuclei, $F(Z', p_e)$ enhances low-energy $\beta^-$ emission and suppresses low-energy $\beta^+$ emission.

\\lambda_\\beta.name: Beta Decay Rate
\\lambda_\\beta.description: Total weak transition probability per unit time.

p_e.name: Electron Momentum
p_e.description: Relativistic linear momentum magnitude of the emitted beta electron.

G_F.name: Fermi Coupling Constant
G_F.description: Low-energy weak interaction coupling strength ($G_F / (\hbar c)^3 \approx 1.166 \times 10^{-5}$ GeV$^{-2}$).

V_{ud}.name: Up-Down CKM Matrix Element
V_{ud}.description: Quark-mixing amplitude coupling up and down quarks in nuclear beta transitions ($|V_{ud}| \approx 0.9737$).

\\mathcal{M}_{fi}.name: Nuclear Transition Matrix Element
\\mathcal{M}_{fi}.description: Dimensionless overlap integral between initial and final nuclear wavefunctions under the weak operator.

F(Z', p_e).name: Coulomb Fermi Function
F(Z', p_e).description: Dimensionless factor correcting the outgoing electron density at the nucleus for electrostatic attraction or repulsion by daughter charge $Z'$.

Q_\\beta.name: Beta Decay Endpoint Energy
Q_\\beta.description: Total kinetic energy available to the emitted electron and antineutrino.

T_e.name: Electron Kinetic Energy
T_e.description: Kinetic energy carried away by the emitted beta electron.

\\hbar.name: Reduced Planck Constant
\\hbar.description: Quantum of action setting the phase-space volume scale.

c.name: Speed of Light
c.description: Relativistic invariant speed entering the massless neutrino dispersion relation.

formulas.title: Allowed Fermi and Gamow-Teller Rate and Sargent's Fifth-Power Law
formulas.description: Expresses the integrated allowed nuclear beta-decay rate as the incoherent sum of vector Fermi ($\Delta J = 0$) and axial-vector Gamow-Teller ($\Delta J = 0, \pm 1$, no $0 \to 0$) nuclear matrix elements multiplied by Sargent's fifth-power phase-space scaling $Q_\beta^5$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Sargent's law and the Fermi/Gamow-Teller decomposition separate nuclear structure overlaps from relativistic three-body phase space, explaining why allowed beta rates scale steeply with endpoint energy.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Doubling the energy released in a fast beta decay speeds up the decay by roughly a factor of thirty-two, while nuclear spin and isospin rules select whether vector or axial-vector transitions contribute.
formulas.interpretation: In the ultra-relativistic limit $Q_\beta \gg m_e c^2$, integrating $p_e^2 (Q_\beta - T_e)^2 dp_e$ gives $Q_\beta^5 / (30 c^3)$. Because $L = 0$ lepton wavefunctions are spatially constant across the nucleus, the vector current drives Fermi transitions ($\mathcal{M}_F$, $g_V = 1$, $\Delta J = 0, \Delta\pi = 0$) and the axial-vector current drives Gamow-Teller transitions ($\mathcal{M}_{GT}$, $g_A \approx -1.276$, $\Delta J = 0, \pm 1$ excluding $0 \to 0$, $\Delta\pi = 0$).
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows from conserved vector current (CVC) isospin symmetry protecting $g_V = 1$, partially conserved axial current (PCAC) renormalization of $g_A$, and rotational/parity invariance of $L = 0$ allowed transitions.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Pure $0^+ \to 0^+$ superallowed transitions have $\mathcal{M}_{GT} = 0$ and provide the most precise determination of $|V_{ud}|$. When $Q_\beta \ll m_e c^2$ (as in tritium decay), non-relativistic phase space softens the scaling toward $Q_\beta^{7/2}$.

\\lambda_\\beta.name: Total Allowed Beta Decay Rate
\\lambda_\\beta.description: Integrated weak transition rate over the full electron momentum spectrum.

G_F.name: Fermi Coupling Constant
G_F.description: Universal low-energy charged-current weak coupling constant.

g_V.name: Vector Weak Coupling
g_V.description: Dimensionless vector coupling constant protected by conserved vector current symmetry ($g_V = 1$).

\\mathcal{M}_F.name: Fermi Nuclear Matrix Element
\\mathcal{M}_F.description: Isospin-ladder overlap governing singlet-lepton ($\Delta J = 0, \Delta\pi = 0$) allowed transitions.

g_A.name: Axial-Vector Weak Coupling
g_A.description: Dimensionless nucleon axial-vector coupling renormalized by QCD ($g_A \approx -1.276$).

\\mathcal{M}_{GT}.name: Gamow-Teller Nuclear Matrix Element
\\mathcal{M}_{GT}.description: Spin-isospin overlap governing triplet-lepton ($\Delta J = 0, \pm 1$ excluding $0 \to 0, \Delta\pi = 0$) allowed transitions.

Q_\\beta.name: Beta Endpoint Energy
Q_\\beta.description: Maximum kinetic energy shared by the electron and antineutrino.

formulas.title: Wu Parity-Violating Beta-Emission Angular Distribution
formulas.description: Gives the normalized angular emission intensity $W(\theta)$ of beta electrons with velocity $\mathbf{v}_e$ emitted from polarized nuclei of mean spin $\langle \mathbf{J} \rangle$, containing the parity-odd pseudoscalar correlation $A_\beta \langle \mathbf{J} \rangle \cdot \mathbf{v}_e / (J c)$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The beta-asymmetry angular distribution directly measures spatial parity violation in weak decays through the correlation between an axial nuclear spin vector and a polar electron velocity vector.
formulas.intuitive_summary: When radioactive cobalt-60 nuclei are lined up like tiny spinning tops, electrons fly out predominantly opposite to the spin direction, proving that the weak force distinguishes left from right.
formulas.interpretation: In Wu's 1957 experiment on polarized $^{60}\text{Co}$ ($5^+ \to 4^+$ pure Gamow-Teller transition), measuring $A_\beta \approx -1$ showed that electrons are emitted antiparallel to $\langle \mathbf{J} \rangle$ with maximal strength $v_e / c$, fixing the left-handed $V - A$ chiral projector $(1 - \gamma_5)/2$ in weak charged currents.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Explicitly breaks discrete spatial inversion symmetry $\mathcal{P}$ (under which $\mathbf{J} \to +\mathbf{J}$ while $\mathbf{v}_e \to -\mathbf{v}_e$), reflecting the chiral $SU(2)_L$ gauge structure of the Standard Model electroweak sector.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: For unpolarized nuclei ($\langle \mathbf{J} \rangle = 0$) or parity-conserving interactions ($A_\beta = 0$), emission is strictly isotropic ($W(\theta) = 1$). In the relativistic limit $v_e / c \to 1$ with full nuclear polarization ($|\langle \mathbf{J} \rangle| = J$) and $A_\beta = -1$, emission parallel to spin ($\theta = 0$) vanishes completely.

W(\\theta).name: Normalized Angular Emission Intensity
W(\\theta).description: Relative probability density for beta-electron emission at angle $\theta$ relative to the nuclear polarization axis.

A_\\beta.name: Beta Asymmetry Parameter
A_\\beta.description: Dimensionless parity-violation coefficient ($A_\beta = -1$ for pure $J \to J-1$ Gamow-Teller $\beta^-$ transitions such as $^{60}$Co).

\\langle \\mathbf{J} \\rangle.name: Nuclear Spin Expectation Vector
\\langle \\mathbf{J} \\rangle.description: Ensemble-averaged nuclear angular momentum vector aligned by cryogenic magnetic polarization.

\\mathbf{v}_e.name: Electron Velocity Vector
\\mathbf{v}_e.description: Polar velocity vector of the emitted beta electron.

J.name: Nuclear Spin Magnitude
J.description: Maximum projection of the parent nuclear spin angular momentum ($J = 5\hbar$ for $^{60}$Co).

c.name: Speed of Light
c.description: Relativistic speed normalizing the electron velocity into the dimensionless ratio $\beta = v_e / c$.

formulas.title: Electromagnetic Gamma-Ray Multipole Parity and Spin Selection Rules
formulas.description: Specifies the exact conservation of parity $\pi_i \pi_f$ and angular momentum $J_i, J_f$ governing nuclear electromagnetic de-excitation via electric ($E\ell$) and magnetic ($M\ell$) multipole photons of order $\ell \ge 1$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Gamma multipole selection rules classify allowed nuclear radiative transitions by matching the angular momentum and intrinsic parity of vector spherical harmonics to the initial and final nuclear states.
formulas.intuitive_summary: A gamma-ray photon carries away integer angular momentum and either flips or preserves nuclear parity depending on whether the radiation is electric or magnetic, strongly favoring the lowest allowed multipole.
formulas.interpretation: Expanding the electromagnetic vector potential in vector spherical harmonics assigns parity $(-1)^\ell$ to electric $E\ell$ multipoles and $(-1)^{\ell+1}$ to magnetic $M\ell$ multipoles. Together with the Weisskopf single-particle rate scaling $\lambda(E\ell) \propto (E_\gamma R / \hbar c)^{2\ell}$, the lowest allowed $\ell$ dominates unless collective quadrupole ($E2$) enhancement competes with $M1$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows directly from rotational invariance $SO(3)$ and exact spatial parity conservation $\mathcal{P}$ of quantum electrodynamics.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Because real transverse photons carry spin 1, $\ell = 0$ single-photon emission is strictly forbidden ($0 \to 0$ transitions must proceed via internal conversion, pair production, or two-photon emission). High multipolarities ($\ell \ge 3$) suppress $\lambda_\gamma$ by many orders of magnitude, creating metastable nuclear isomers.

\\pi_i.name: Initial Nuclear Parity
\\pi_i.description: Intrinsic parity eigenvalue ($+1$ or $-1$) of the excited initial nuclear state.

\\pi_f.name: Final Nuclear Parity
\\pi_f.description: Intrinsic parity eigenvalue ($+1$ or $-1$) of the lower-energy final nuclear state.

\\ell.name: Photon Multipole Order
\\ell.description: Integer total angular momentum quantum number ($\ell \ge 1$) carried away by the emitted gamma photon.

J_i.name: Initial Nuclear Spin
J_i.description: Total angular momentum quantum number of the excited initial nuclear level.

J_f.name: Final Nuclear Spin
J_f.description: Total angular momentum quantum number of the final nuclear level.

formulas.title: Nuclear Reaction Q-Value and Mass-Defect Energy Release
formulas.description: Quantifies the net kinetic energy released ($Q > 0$, exothermic) or absorbed ($Q < 0$, endothermic) in a nuclear reaction from the difference between the total rest mass of initial reactants $\sum m_i$ and final products $\sum m_f$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The nuclear reaction Q-value converts the change in nuclear binding energy between reactants and products into relativistic kinetic energy via mass-energy equivalence.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Whenever a nuclear rearrangement binds nucleons more tightly, the final nuclei weigh slightly less than the starting nuclei, and that missing mass emerges as kinetic energy.
formulas.interpretation: For thermal-neutron fission of $^{235}\text{U}$, the mass defect of roughly $0.215\,\text{u}$ releases $Q \approx 200\,\text{MeV}$, carried mostly by the Coulomb-accelerated fission fragments. For D-T fusion, a mass defect of $0.0189\,\text{u}$ releases $Q = 17.6\,\text{MeV}$, partitioned inversely by mass into a $3.52\,\text{MeV}$ alpha particle and a $14.08\,\text{MeV}$ neutron.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows directly from time-translation invariance and Lorentz four-momentum conservation applied to relativistic bound nuclear states.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: For elastic scattering ($\sum m_f = \sum m_i$), $Q = 0$. When $Q < 0$, the reaction requires an incident center-of-mass kinetic energy exceeding the threshold $|Q|$.

Q.name: Nuclear Reaction Q-Value
Q.description: Net kinetic energy released (positive) or absorbed (negative) in a nuclear reaction.

m_i.name: Initial Reactant Rest Mass
m_i.description: Rest mass of each incoming nuclear or particle species before reaction.

m_f.name: Final Product Rest Mass
m_f.description: Rest mass of each outgoing nuclear or particle species after reaction.

c.name: Speed of Light in Vacuum
c.description: Universal relativistic conversion constant relating mass defect to energy.

formulas.title: Breit-Wigner Resonant Neutron-Induced Fission Cross Section
formulas.description: Gives the single-level resonant cross section $\sigma_{n,f}(E)$ for a neutron of center-of-mass kinetic energy $E$ and wavenumber $k$ to form a compound nucleus of resonance energy $E_0$ and total width $\Gamma$ that decays via fission.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The Breit-Wigner formula describes the Lorentzian energy profile of compound-nucleus formation and subsequent fission decay near an isolated quasi-stationary nuclear level.
formulas.intuitive_summary: When an incoming neutron matches the exact excitation energy of a compound nucleus, the probability of capture and fission spikes sharply like a tuned acoustic resonator.
formulas.interpretation: In partial-wave scattering theory, the maximum s-wave geometric cross section is $\pi/k^2$, weighted by the spin statistical factor $g_J = (2J+1)/[(2s_n+1)(2I+1)]$ and the branching product $\Gamma_n \Gamma_f / \Gamma^2$ at peak ($E = E_0$). For low-energy s-wave neutrons, $\Gamma_n \propto v$ while $k^{-2} \propto v^{-2}$, generating the famous $1/v$ thermal-neutron capture enhancement.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Arises from unitarity of the quantum S-matrix and angular-momentum conservation in isolated compound-nucleus scattering channels.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: At exact resonance ($E = E_0$), $\sigma_{n,f}(E_0) = (4\pi g_J / k^2)(\Gamma_n \Gamma_f / \Gamma^2)$. Far below resonance ($E \ll E_0$), $\sigma_{n,f}(E) \propto 1/v$ because $\Gamma_n \propto \sqrt{E}$ and $k^2 \propto E$.

\\sigma_{n,f}.name: Neutron-Induced Fission Cross Section
\\sigma_{n,f}.description: Effective nuclear target area for neutron capture followed by fission.

k.name: Center-of-Mass Neutron Wavenumber
k.description: De Broglie wavenumber $k = \sqrt{2\mu E}/\hbar$ of the incident neutron-nucleus system.

g_J.name: Spin Statistical Factor
g_J.description: Dimensionless angular-momentum multiplicity weight for forming a compound state of total spin $J$.

\\Gamma_n.name: Neutron Entrance Partial Width
\\Gamma_n.description: Energy width governing elastic neutron emission from the compound nucleus.

\\Gamma_f.name: Fission Decay Partial Width
\\Gamma_f.description: Energy width governing scission of the compound nucleus into fission fragments.

E.name: Center-of-Mass Kinetic Energy
E.description: Kinetic energy of the incident neutron-nucleus pair in the center-of-mass frame.

E_0.name: Compound-Nucleus Resonance Energy
E_0.description: Excitation energy of the isolated quasi-bound compound nuclear level.

\\Gamma.name: Total Resonance Width
\\Gamma.description: Full energy width $\Gamma = \hbar/\tau$ summing all open decay channels of the compound state.

formulas.title: Four-Factor and Effective Neutron Multiplication Formula
formulas.equation: k_{\mathrm{eff}} = k_\infty P_{\mathrm{NL}} = \eta f p \varepsilon P_{\mathrm{NL}}
formulas.description: Expresses the effective neutron multiplication factor $k_{\mathrm{eff}}$ of a finite thermal fission reactor as the product of the infinite-medium four-factor formula $k_\infty = \eta f p \varepsilon$ and the geometric non-leakage probability $P_{\mathrm{NL}}$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The six-factor criticality balance tracks the survival and regeneration of one complete generation of thermal neutrons from fission birth through slowing down to the next fission event.
formulas.intuitive_summary: A reactor stays steady when each fission produces exactly one surviving neutron that triggers a subsequent fission after accounting for moderation losses, parasitic absorption, and escape from the core.
formulas.interpretation: Each dimensionless factor isolates a distinct physical stage: $\eta$ gives fission neutrons per thermal absorption in fuel, $f$ is the fraction of thermal neutrons absorbed in fuel rather than moderator or structure, $p$ is the probability of escaping $^{238}\text{U}$ epithermal capture resonances, $\varepsilon$ accounts for extra fast-neutron fissions, and $P_{\mathrm{NL}}$ measures retention inside the finite core.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows from steady-state neutron-number conservation in the linear Boltzmann transport equation for a multiplying medium.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: The reactor is subcritical for $k_{\mathrm{eff}} < 1$, exactly critical for $k_{\mathrm{eff}} = 1$, and supercritical for $k_{\mathrm{eff}} > 1$. In an infinitely large core, $P_{\mathrm{NL}} \to 1$ and $k_{\mathrm{eff}} \to k_\infty$.

k_{\\mathrm{eff}}.name: Effective Multiplication Factor
k_{\\mathrm{eff}}.description: Ratio of neutron population in one generation to the preceding generation in a finite reactor core.

k_\\infty.name: Infinite Multiplication Factor
k_\\infty.description: Multiplication factor of an infinite, leakage-free reactor lattice.

P_{\\mathrm{NL}}.name: Non-Leakage Probability
P_{\\mathrm{NL}}.description: Probability that a fission neutron remains inside the finite core during slowing down and thermal diffusion.

\\eta.name: Thermal Reproduction Factor
\\eta.description: Average number of fast fission neutrons produced per thermal neutron absorbed in nuclear fuel.

f.name: Thermal Utilization Factor
f.description: Fraction of absorbed thermal neutrons captured by fuel rather than moderator or structural materials.

p.name: Resonance Escape Probability
p.description: Probability that a slowing neutron avoids non-fission resonance capture before reaching thermal energy.

\\varepsilon.name: Fast Fission Factor
\\varepsilon.description: Ratio of total fission neutrons (fast plus thermal) to those produced by thermal fission alone.

formulas.title: Delayed-Neutron Effective Generation Time
formulas.description: Computes the mean effective neutron generation time $\ell_{\mathrm{eff}}$ in a fission reactor by weighting the prompt neutron lifetime $\ell_p$ against the delayed-neutron precursor lifetime $\bar{\tau}_d$ with delayed fraction $\beta$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The effective generation time averages prompt and beta-decay-delayed fission neutrons to establish the sluggish kinetic response time that makes nuclear reactors mechanically controllable.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Even though less than one percent of fission neutrons arrive seconds late, those stragglers dominate the average generation time and slow reactor power swings from milliseconds to tens of seconds.
formulas.interpretation: In $^{235}\text{U}$ thermal reactors, $\ell_p \sim 10^{-4}\,\text{s}$, $\beta \approx 0.0065$, and $\bar{\tau}_d \approx 13\,\text{s}$, so the delayed term $\beta \bar{\tau}_d \approx 0.085\,\text{s}$ exceeds the prompt term by nearly three orders of magnitude. As long as reactivity $\rho < \beta$, the reactor period scales as $\ell_{\mathrm{eff}}/\rho$, giving control systems ample time to respond.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Derived from the coupled point-kinetics neutron and delayed-precursor balance equations in the small-reactivity ($\rho \ll \beta$) adiabatic limit.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: If $\beta \to 0$ (no delayed neutrons), $\ell_{\mathrm{eff}} \to \ell_p$. When reactivity exceeds $\beta$ (prompt criticality), the prompt chain becomes self-sustaining independently and power rises on the microsecond-to-millisecond timescale $\ell_p/(\rho - \beta)$.

\\ell_{\\mathrm{eff}}.name: Effective Neutron Generation Time
\\ell_{\\mathrm{eff}}.description: Weighted average time between successive neutron generations including delayed precursors.

\\beta.name: Delayed Neutron Fraction
\\beta.description: Fraction of fission neutrons emitted following beta decay of neutron-rich fission products ($\approx 0.0065$ for $^{235}\text{U}$).

\\ell_p.name: Prompt Neutron Lifetime
\\ell_p.description: Mean time from prompt fission emission to subsequent absorption in the reactor core.

\\bar{\\tau}_d.name: Mean Delayed-Precursor Lifetime
\\bar{\\tau}_d.description: Weighted average beta-decay lifetime of delayed-neutron precursor nuclei ($\approx 13\,\text{s}$).

formulas.title: Gamow-Peak Thermonuclear Reactivity Integral
formulas.description: Evaluates the thermal-averaged fusion reactivity $\langle \sigma v \rangle$ by integrating the nuclear astrophysical factor $S(E)$ over the product of the Maxwell-Boltzmann energy distribution and the WKB Coulomb-barrier tunneling factor $\exp(-\sqrt{E_G/E})$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The thermonuclear reactivity integral quantifies the fusion rate coefficient per unit ion-density product in a hot plasma by balancing exponentially rare high-energy ions against exponentially rising quantum tunneling probability.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Most plasma ions are too slow to penetrate electrical repulsion while the fastest ions are too scarce, so almost all fusion occurs inside a narrow middle energy window called the Gamow peak.
formulas.interpretation: Factoring the fusion cross section as $\sigma(E) = S(E) E^{-1} \exp(-\sqrt{E_G/E})$ separates smooth nuclear-structure physics in $S(E)$ from the steep Coulomb barrier governed by the Gamow energy $E_G = 2\mu c^2(\pi \alpha Z_1 Z_2)^2$. Saddle-point integration locates the Gamow peak at $E_0 = [(k_B T)^2 E_G / 4]^{1/3}$, well above the mean thermal energy $k_B T$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Combines Maxwell-Boltzmann statistical equilibrium of an isotropic thermal plasma with WKB quantum tunneling across a spherically symmetric $1/r$ Coulomb potential.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: At low temperatures ($k_B T \ll E_G$), reactivity rises exponentially with temperature as $T^{-2/3} \exp[-3(E_G/(4 k_B T))^{1/3}]$. For D-T fusion, a broad $^5\text{He}$ resonance peaks $\langle \sigma v \rangle$ near $k_B T \approx 65\,\text{keV}$.

\\langle \\sigma v \\rangle.name: Thermonuclear Reactivity
\\langle \\sigma v \\rangle.description: Maxwellian-averaged product of fusion cross section and relative ion velocity.

\\mu.name: Reduced Mass of Reacting Nuclei
\\mu.description: Two-body reduced mass $\mu = m_1 m_2 / (m_1 + m_2)$ of the fusing ion pair.

k_B.name: Boltzmann Constant
k_B.description: Conversion factor relating thermodynamic temperature to thermal energy.

T.name: Plasma Ion Temperature
T.description: Thermodynamic temperature characterizing the Maxwell-Boltzmann ion velocity distribution.

S(E).name: Astrophysical S-Factor
S(E).description: Slowly varying nuclear-physics factor remaining after removing geometric $1/E$ and Coulomb tunneling factors from $\sigma(E)$.

E.name: Center-of-Mass Collision Energy
E.description: Relative kinetic energy of the colliding nuclei in their center-of-mass frame.

E_G.name: Gamow Energy
E_G.description: Characteristic Coulomb-barrier energy scale $E_G = 2\mu c^2 (\pi \alpha Z_1 Z_2)^2$.

formulas.title: Lawson Triple-Product Ignition Criterion
formulas.equation: n T \tau_E \ge \frac{12 k_B T^2}{\langle \sigma v \rangle E_\alpha}
formulas.description: Establishes the minimum fusion triple product $n T \tau_E$ of plasma density $n$, temperature $T$, and energy confinement time $\tau_E$ required for alpha-particle self-heating to sustain a burning D-T plasma without external power.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The Lawson triple-product criterion condenses steady-state thermonuclear power balance into a single figure of merit separating externally driven plasmas from self-sustaining ignited burn.
formulas.intuitive_summary: For a fusion plasma to keep itself hot without external heaters, its density, temperature, and heat-retention time multiplied together must cross a sharp threshold set by the fuel's reactivity.
formulas.interpretation: In an equimolar D-T plasma ($n_D = n_T = n/2$), alpha-particle heating power density $\frac{1}{4} n^2 \langle \sigma v \rangle E_\alpha$ must equal or exceed conductive-transport loss $3 n k_B T / \tau_E$. Minimizing $T^2/\langle \sigma v \rangle$ selects the optimal operating window $k_B T \approx 14\text{--}15\,\text{keV}$, yielding $n T \tau_E \ge 3 \times 10^{21}\,\text{keV}\cdot\text{s}\cdot\text{m}^{-3}$ once bremsstrahlung radiation losses are included.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows from global steady-state energy conservation balancing internal charged-particle fusion deposition against thermal transport losses.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: At very low temperatures ($k_B T < 4.3\,\text{keV}$), bremsstrahlung radiation exceeds D-T alpha heating regardless of $\tau_E$, making ignition impossible. At very high temperatures ($k_B T > 50\,\text{keV}$), $T^2/\langle \sigma v \rangle$ rises again and raises the required triple product.

n.name: Total Fuel Ion Number Density
n.description: Combined deuterium-tritium ion number density ($n = n_D + n_T$) in the burning plasma.

T.name: Plasma Temperature
T.description: Thermodynamic temperature of the confined fusion plasma.

\\tau_E.name: Energy Confinement Time
\\tau_E.description: Characteristic timescale over which stored plasma thermal energy leaks out via transport.

k_B.name: Boltzmann Constant
k_B.description: Relates thermodynamic temperature to mean particle thermal energy.

E_\\alpha.name: Alpha-Particle Fusion Energy
E_\\alpha.description: Kinetic energy ($3.52\,\text{MeV}$) carried by the $^4\text{He}$ product that remains confined to self-heat the plasma.

formulas.title: Fusion Energy Gain Factor and Burning-Plasma Power Balance
formulas.description: Defines the plasma fusion energy gain factor $Q_{\mathrm{fus}}$ as the ratio of total fusion power $P_{\mathrm{fus}}$ to external auxiliary heating power $P_{\mathrm{aux}}$, expressed for D-T fuel in terms of alpha self-heating $P_\alpha$ and total power loss $P_{\mathrm{loss}}$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The fusion energy gain factor measures how much thermonuclear power a reactor produces per unit of external heating supplied to sustain the plasma.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Gain equals one at scientific breakeven, reaches five when internal alpha particles match external heaters, and shoots to infinity at ignition when external heating can be turned off.
formulas.interpretation: Because D-T fusion deposits one-fifth of its $17.6\,\text{MeV}$ yield into confined $3.52\,\text{MeV}$ alpha particles ($P_{\mathrm{fus}} = 5 P_\alpha$) while steady-state power balance enforces $P_{\mathrm{aux}} + P_\alpha = P_{\mathrm{loss}}$, the gain diverges as $P_\alpha \to P_{\mathrm{loss}}$. ITER is engineered for $Q_{\mathrm{fus}} = 10$ ($500\,\text{MW}$ fusion from $50\,\text{MW}$ auxiliary drive), whereas NIF achieved $Q_{\mathrm{fus}} \approx 1.54$ target gain in December 2022.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows directly from steady-state macroscopic energy balance across the burning plasma control volume.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: At $Q_{\mathrm{fus}} = 1$ (scientific breakeven), $P_{\mathrm{fus}} = P_{\mathrm{aux}}$. At $Q_{\mathrm{fus}} = 5$ (burning-plasma onset), $P_\alpha = P_{\mathrm{aux}}$. As $P_\alpha \to P_{\mathrm{loss}}$ (ignition), $P_{\mathrm{aux}} \to 0$ and $Q_{\mathrm{fus}} \to \infty$.

Q_{\\mathrm{fus}}.name: Fusion Energy Gain Factor
Q_{\\mathrm{fus}}.description: Dimensionless ratio of generated fusion power to external heating power delivered to the plasma.

P_{\\mathrm{fus}}.name: Total Fusion Power
P_{\\mathrm{fus}}.description: Total thermal power released by D-T fusion reactions (neutrons plus alpha particles).

P_{\\mathrm{aux}}.name: Auxiliary External Heating Power
P_{\\mathrm{aux}}.description: External heating power supplied via neutral beams, radiofrequency waves, or laser drive.

P_\\alpha.name: Alpha-Particle Self-Heating Power
P_\\alpha.description: Fraction ($P_{\mathrm{fus}}/5$) of fusion power deposited directly back into the plasma by confined alpha particles.

P_{\\mathrm{loss}}.name: Total Plasma Power Loss
P_{\\mathrm{loss}}.description: Combined conductive, convective, and radiative (bremsstrahlung) power escaping the plasma.

formulas.title: Nuclear Magnetic Moment and Larmor Precession Frequency
formulas.description: Relates a nucleus's magnetic dipole moment operator $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ to its dimensionless spin angular momentum operator $\mathbf{I}$ via the isotope-specific gyromagnetic ratio $\gamma$, and determines the Larmor angular precession frequency $\omega_0$ in a static magnetic field $B_0$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Every nucleus with nonzero spin behaves as a quantized magnetic gyroscope whose dipole moment scales linearly with spin and precesses around an applied magnetic field at a frequency strictly proportional to field strength.
formulas.intuitive_summary: A spinning atomic nucleus acts like a tiny compass needle that wobbles around a static magnetic field at a fixed pitch determined by the isotope and the magnet strength.
formulas.interpretation: In the Zeeman Hamiltonian $H = -\boldsymbol{\mu} \cdot \mathbf{B}_0 = -\gamma \hbar B_0 I_z$, adjacent magnetic sublevels ($\Delta m_I = \pm 1$) are separated by $\Delta E = \hbar \omega_0 = \gamma \hbar B_0$. For $^1\mathrm{H}$, $\gamma/(2\pi) = 42.577\,\mathrm{MHz/T}$, placing proton NMR in the 400–1200 MHz radiofrequency band inside superconducting magnets.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows from the Wigner-Eckart theorem under $SO(3)$ rotational symmetry, which forces the dipole vector operator within a fixed-spin manifold $I$ to be proportional to $\mathbf{I}$, combined with Heisenberg evolution under the Zeeman interaction.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Applies to isolated spins in a uniform static field $B_0$ when quadrupole and hyperfine couplings are small compared to the Zeeman energy. As $B_0 \to 0$, Zeeman splitting vanishes and internal dipolar or quadrupolar interactions dominate.

\\boldsymbol{\\mu}.name: Nuclear Magnetic Dipole Moment
\\boldsymbol{\\mu}.description: Vector magnetic dipole moment operator of an atomic nucleus.

\\gamma.name: Nuclear Gyromagnetic Ratio
\\gamma.description: Isotope-specific ratio of magnetic moment to angular momentum, proportional to the nuclear g-factor.

\\mathbf{I}.name: Nuclear Spin Operator
\\mathbf{I}.description: Dimensionless nuclear spin angular momentum operator with eigenvalues $\sqrt{I(I+1)}$ and $m_I$.

\\omega_0.name: Larmor Angular Frequency
\\omega_0.description: Resonant angular frequency of nuclear spin precession around the static magnetic field.

B_0.name: Static Magnetic Flux Density
B_0.description: Magnitude of the applied homogeneous static magnetic field.

formulas.title: Bloch Equations for Nuclear Magnetization Dynamics
formulas.description: Governs the time evolution of the macroscopic nuclear magnetization vector $\mathbf{M}(t)$ under a time-dependent magnetic field $\mathbf{B}(t)$, combining coherent Larmor torque with longitudinal spin-lattice relaxation $T_1$ and transverse spin-spin dephasing $T_2$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The Bloch equations model an ensemble of weakly coupled nuclear spins as a classical magnetization vector precessing under applied fields while exponentially relaxing toward thermal equilibrium along $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ and dephasing in the transverse plane.
formulas.intuitive_summary: A sample's net nuclear magnetism spirals back toward alignment with the main magnet while its sideways wobble fades out as individual spins fall out of step.
formulas.interpretation: The cross-product term $\gamma \mathbf{M} \times \mathbf{B}(t)$ drives unitary Larmor precession and resonant radiofrequency nutation. The $T_1$ term restores $M_z$ to the Curie equilibrium value $M_0$ via energy exchange with the lattice, while the $T_2$ term damps $M_x$ and $M_y$ through both energy-conserving secular dephasing and $T_1$ processes, enforcing $T_2 \le 2 T_1$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Combines $SO(3)$ spin-precession dynamics with axial $SO(2)$ rotational symmetry around the static field axis $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ and Markovian thermal bath coupling.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: In the limit $T_1, T_2 \to \infty$, the equations reduce to dissipationless Larmor precession conserving $|\mathbf{M}|$. Strictly valid for non-interacting or weakly coupled spin-half ensembles in liquids; strong dipolar coupling in solids requires density-matrix generalizations.

\\mathbf{M}.name: Macroscopic Nuclear Magnetization
\\mathbf{M}.description: Net nuclear magnetic dipole moment per unit volume.

\\gamma.name: Nuclear Gyromagnetic Ratio
\\gamma.description: Isotope-specific gyromagnetic ratio linking torque to magnetization.

\\mathbf{B}(t).name: Total Applied Magnetic Field
\\mathbf{B}(t).description: Sum of the static field $B_0 \hat{\mathbf{z}}$ and transverse radiofrequency excitation fields.

T_1.name: Spin-Lattice Relaxation Time
T_1.description: Characteristic time constant for longitudinal magnetization $M_z$ to recover thermal equilibrium $M_0$.

T_2.name: Spin-Spin Relaxation Time
T_2.description: Characteristic time constant for irreversible decay of transverse phase coherence.

formulas.title: NMR Chemical Shift and Electronic Shielding
formulas.description: Defines the dimensionless, field-independent chemical shift $\delta$ (commonly reported in parts per million) from the resonance frequency $\nu$ of a nucleus relative to a reference compound $\nu_{\mathrm{ref}}$, expressed in terms of isotropic electronic shielding constants $\sigma$ and $\sigma_{\mathrm{ref}}$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Electronic orbital currents induced by the external field partially screen each nucleus as $B_{\mathrm{loc}} = (1 - \sigma) B_0$, shifting its Larmor frequency by a fractional amount $\delta$ that serves as a field-independent fingerprint of chemical bonding.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Nearby electrons act like a tiny magnetic umbrella around each nucleus, nudging its resonance frequency by a few parts per million in a way that reveals its exact chemical neighborhood.
formulas.interpretation: Because both $\nu = (\gamma/2\pi)(1 - \sigma)B_0$ and $\nu_{\mathrm{ref}} = (\gamma/2\pi)(1 - \sigma_{\mathrm{ref}})B_0$ scale linearly with $B_0$, their fractional difference cancels the spectrometer field strength. Since $|\sigma_{\mathrm{ref}}| \ll 1$, $\delta \approx \sigma_{\mathrm{ref}} - \sigma$, so more deshielded nuclei resonate at higher $\delta$ (downfield).
formulas.symmetry_origin: Arises from gauge-invariant orbital current response of molecular electrons to a uniform magnetic field, averaged isotropically over rapid molecular tumbling in solution.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid in isotropic liquids where rapid tumbling averages the full chemical shielding tensor $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ to its trace $\sigma = \frac{1}{3}\mathrm{Tr}(\boldsymbol{\sigma})$. In solids, orientation-dependent chemical shift anisotropy broadens lines unless averaged by magic-angle spinning.

\\delta.name: Chemical Shift
\\delta.description: Dimensionless relative resonance frequency shift, conventionally expressed in parts per million (ppm).

\\nu.name: Sample Resonance Frequency
\\nu.description: Measured Larmor frequency of the target nucleus in its chemical environment.

\\nu_{\\mathrm{ref}}.name: Reference Resonance Frequency
\\nu_{\\mathrm{ref}}.description: Resonance frequency of a standard reference nucleus such as tetramethylsilane (TMS).

\\sigma.name: Isotropic Nuclear Shielding Constant
\\sigma.description: Dimensionless fractional reduction of the local magnetic field at the sample nucleus due to orbital electrons.

\\sigma_{\\mathrm{ref}}.name: Reference Shielding Constant
\\sigma_{\\mathrm{ref}}.description: Dimensionless isotropic electronic shielding constant of the reference compound.

formulas.title: MRI Linear Magnetic Field Gradient Spatial Encoding
formulas.description: Maps spatial position $\mathbf{r}$ linearly onto nuclear Larmor precession frequency $\omega(\mathbf{r})$ by superposing a controlled magnetic field gradient $\mathbf{G} = \nabla B_z$ onto the static main field $B_0$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Applying a uniform magnetic field gradient tags every voxel of a macroscopic object with a unique precession frequency and accumulated phase, enabling Fourier reconstruction of internal nuclear spin density.
formulas.intuitive_summary: By tilting the magnetic field slightly from one side of the body to the other, spins at different locations sing at slightly different radio frequencies so a computer can reconstruct a three-dimensional image.
formulas.interpretation: In the rotating frame demodulated at $\omega_0 = \gamma B_0$, the accumulated phase $\phi(\mathbf{r}, t) = \gamma \int_0^t \mathbf{G}(t') \cdot \mathbf{r}\,dt' = \mathbf{k}(t) \cdot \mathbf{r}$ defines the spatial-frequency trajectory $\mathbf{k}(t)$, turning the detected induction voltage into the direct Fourier transform of the transverse magnetization distribution.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Deliberately breaks spatial translation invariance of the static field along the gradient axis $\mathbf{G}$ so position becomes conjugate to reciprocal wavevector $\mathbf{k}$ via Fourier duality.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Requires $|\mathbf{G} \cdot \mathbf{r}| \ll B_0$ so concomitant transverse Maxwell gradient components remain negligible. Spatial resolution improves with larger integrated gradient area $|\mathbf{k}_{\max}|$, bounded by $T_2^*$ decay and signal-to-noise ratio.

\\omega(\\mathbf{r}).name: Position-Dependent Larmor Frequency
\\omega(\\mathbf{r}).description: Local nuclear spin precession angular frequency at spatial coordinate $\mathbf{r}$.

\\gamma.name: Nuclear Gyromagnetic Ratio
\\gamma.description: Gyromagnetic ratio of the imaged nuclear species, typically $^1\mathrm{H}$ protons.

B_0.name: Static Main Magnetic Field
B_0.description: Homogeneous background magnetic flux density at the scanner isocenter.

\\mathbf{G}.name: Magnetic Field Gradient Vector
\\mathbf{G}.description: Spatial gradient $\nabla B_z$ of the longitudinal magnetic field component.

\\mathbf{r}.name: Spatial Position Vector
\\mathbf{r}.description: Three-dimensional displacement from the magnet isocenter.

formulas.title: Free-Nucleus Gamma-Ray Recoil Energy
formulas.description: Gives the non-relativistic kinetic recoil energy $E_R$ imparted to an unbound nucleus of mass $M$ when it emits or absorbs a gamma-ray photon of energy $E_\gamma$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Linear momentum conservation during nuclear gamma emission forces a free nucleus to recoil with momentum $p = E_\gamma/c$, subtracting $E_R = p^2/(2M)$ from the emitted photon energy and shifting emission and absorption lines apart by $2E_R$.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Just as firing a rifle kicks the shooter backward, emitting a high-energy gamma photon kicks a free nucleus backward and steals enough energy to knock it out of resonance with identical nuclei.
formulas.interpretation: Because $E_R \propto E_\gamma^2 / M$, optical atomic transitions ($E_\gamma \sim 2\,\mathrm{eV}$) suffer negligible recoil ($E_R \sim 10^{-11}\,\mathrm{eV} \ll \Gamma$), whereas nuclear transitions like $^{57}\mathrm{Fe}$ ($E_\gamma = 14.4\,\mathrm{keV}$) experience $E_R \approx 1.95\,\mathrm{meV} \gg \Gamma \approx 4.7\,\mathrm{neV}$, blocking resonant absorption in free atoms.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows directly from conservation of relativistic four-momentum under spacetime translation invariance for a two-body nuclear decay.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid in the non-relativistic recoil regime $E_\gamma \ll M c^2$, which holds to better than $10^{-6}$ for all nuclear gamma transitions below several MeV. When the nucleus is bound rigidly to a macroscopic crystal of mass $M_{\mathrm{crystal}} \to \infty$, $E_R \to 0$.

E_R.name: Nuclear Recoil Kinetic Energy
E_R.description: Kinetic energy absorbed by a free nucleus during gamma-ray emission or absorption.

E_\\gamma.name: Gamma-Ray Photon Energy
E_\\gamma.description: Energy of the emitted or absorbed nuclear transition photon.

M.name: Nuclear Mass
M.description: Rest mass of the unbound emitting or absorbing nucleus.

c.name: Speed of Light in Vacuum
c.description: Universal relativistic constant relating photon energy and momentum, $p = E_\gamma/c$.

formulas.title: Lamb-Mössbauer Recoil-Free Fraction
formulas.description: Gives the probability $f$ that a nucleus bound inside a harmonic crystal lattice emits or absorbs a gamma-ray photon of wavenumber $k = E_\gamma/(\hbar c)$ without creating or annihilating any lattice phonons, where $\langle x^2 \rangle$ is the mean-square nuclear vibrational displacement along the propagation axis.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The Lamb-Mössbauer factor is the squared matrix element $|\langle n_i | e^{i k x} | n_i \rangle|^2$ for zero-phonon nuclear gamma transitions, quantifying the fraction of emissions that remain strictly recoil-free at the natural linewidth.
formulas.intuitive_summary: When a nucleus is locked inside a cold, stiff crystal, there is a finite chance the lattice refuses to vibrate at all during gamma emission, letting the whole crystal take the kick so the photon keeps its full energy.
formulas.interpretation: Closely analogous to the X-ray Debye-Waller factor, $f$ approaches unity when the root-mean-square thermal and zero-point displacement $\sqrt{\langle x^2 \rangle}$ is small compared to the reduced gamma wavelength $1/k$. In the Debye model at $T = 0$, $f = \exp(-3 E_R / (2 k_B \Theta_D))$, demonstrating that zero-point motion still bounds $f < 1$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Originates from quantized normal-mode lattice vibrations (phonons) in a discrete translationally invariant crystal and the harmonic-oscillator Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff identity.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid for harmonic lattice potentials; anharmonicity or diffusive motion in liquids drives $\langle x^2 \rangle \to \infty$ and $f \to 0$. For $^{57}\mathrm{Fe}$ in metallic iron at room temperature, $f \approx 0.78$.

f.name: Lamb-Mössbauer Recoil-Free Fraction
f.description: Dimensionless probability of zero-phonon, recoilless gamma-ray emission or absorption.

k.name: Gamma-Ray Wavenumber
k.description: Magnitude of the gamma-ray wavevector, $k = E_\gamma/(\hbar c) = 2\pi/\lambda$.

\\langle x^2 \\rangle.name: Mean-Square Nuclear Displacement
\\langle x^2 \\rangle.description: Thermal and quantum zero-point mean-square vibrational displacement of the nucleus along the gamma-ray propagation direction.

formulas.title: Pound-Rebka Gravitational Redshift Doppler Balance
formulas.description: Equates the weak-field general-relativistic gravitational frequency shift $\Delta \nu / \nu = g h / c^2$ across a vertical height $h$ in uniform gravitational acceleration $g$ to the compensating first-order Doppler shift $v / c$ applied to a Mössbauer gamma-ray source.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Expresses the equivalence-principle compensation condition used in the 1960 Pound-Rebka experiment, where translating a recoilless $^{57}\mathrm{Fe}$ source at speed $v = g h / c$ cancels the gravitational frequency shift across height $h$ and restores resonant absorption.
formulas.intuitive_summary: A gamma ray climbing out of Earth's gravity loses a tiny fraction of its frequency, which can be canceled out by nudging the emitter forward at less than a micrometer per second.
formulas.interpretation: Over Harvard's $h = 22.5\,\mathrm{m}$ Jefferson tower with $g = 9.80\,\mathrm{m/s}^2$, $g h / c^2 \approx 2.46 \times 10^{-15}$, requiring a compensating Doppler speed $v \approx 7.37 \times 10^{-7}\,\mathrm{m/s}$. Reversing source and absorber positions cancels systematic temperature-dependent second-order Doppler shifts.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows directly from Einstein's equivalence principle relating uniform gravitational fields to uniformly accelerated reference frames in the weak-field metric $g_{00} \approx -(1 + 2 g z / c^2)$.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid in the weak, uniform gravitational limit $g h \ll c^2$ and non-relativistic Doppler regime $v \ll c$. For strong fields near compact objects, the exact Schwarzschild factor $\sqrt{(1 - r_s/r_2)/(1 - r_s/r_1)} - 1$ replaces $g h / c^2$.

\\Delta \\nu.name: Frequency Shift
\\Delta \\nu.description: Change in gamma-ray photon frequency between emission and absorption altitudes.

g.name: Local Gravitational Acceleration
g.description: Magnitude of Earth's local gravitational acceleration along the tower.

h.name: Vertical Tower Height
h.description: Vertical separation between the gamma-ray source and absorber.

c.name: Speed of Light in Vacuum
c.description: Universal speed of light in vacuum.

v.name: Compensating Doppler Velocity
v.description: Source translation speed along the propagation axis required to cancel the gravitational shift.
